purpose: Evaluate one fixed content-only lexical ordering on four paired development R0 inputs; not formal evaluation or significance testing.
prediction: Sorting may help if matching places useful evidence earlier; it may not help or may hurt because related distractors can outrank necessary supplement evidence. No rule changes after outcomes.
known_before_calls: Offline rankings and prior development results have already been seen; this is not blind selection or a prediction written before earlier experiments.

runtime.cache_policy: Erase slot cache before each call; use external slot-save-path only for cache management

evaluation_rules: Evaluate full answer/citations JSON schema separately from answer correctness.
Public dev answers used only after model response is saved; not passed to inference or ordering.
Check answer against public aliases and visible original evidence.
Check cited IDs against actual input; absent citations are absent, not silently repaired.
Check semantic sufficiency from quoted source sentences, not ID membership alone.
Record all wrong answers, missing citations and elapsed time; no answer-based retry.

reference_evaluation_logic.numeric_and_choice: Expected necessary evidence IDs must be present; compare original cited text to conclusion, record extras for manual review.
reference_evaluation_logic.insufficient: Require actual inspection sources such as noncollected hardware fields; an empty public evidence list does not justify fabricating or silently adding citations.

stop_conditions: Exactly eight planned calls if service works.
Any transport, HTTP, provider-JSON or service technical failure is saved and stops the sequence; no retry.
Malformed model answer or wrong answer is retained and does not trigger retry.
No ranking/prompt/model/parameter tuning during this fixed sequence.
No formal cases, download, report edits, staging, commit or push.
success_definition: format complete AND answer correct AND citations exist in actual input AND cited text sufficiently supports answer.
reporting: Summarize only four paired cases, including improvements, regressions and no changes; no statistical significance or formal-set claim.
